blocks.x: Agentic AI & Hyperautomation applied to Capabilities. This page sets out the operating context, the delivery pattern we run, the services and platforms involved, and the outcomes we commit to.

In Banking & Financial Services, agentic ai & hyperautomation turns knowledge work into orchestrated autonomy. That is the baseline pattern; the differentiator is what it connects to: agentic process automation, digital workforce & multi-agent orchestration, decision intelligence systems — delivered on Dataq Swarm and Dataq Nexus and Dataq Compass with the sector's regulatory posture built in.

items: KYC and periodic-review backlog

Customer due diligence refresh cycles lag behind actual risk changes; files queue for weeks in review pools while remediation backlogs grow. Manual file assembly across registries, screening tools and core systems consumes analyst hours that produce no judgment.
Fraud and AML decisions too slow

Batch scoring misses the real-time payment window; rules engines generate alert volumes that investigation teams cannot clear. The result is both rising fraud leakage and rising false-positive cost in the same program.
GenAI stuck between pilot and policy

Generative assistants for credit memos, research summaries and client drafts stall in model-risk review because guardrails, provenance and audit trails were not designed in. Shadow AI fills the gap, creating exactly the exposure the review was meant to prevent.

blocks.x: How we deliver it in this sector

The delivery pattern composes 7 services from the Agentic AI & Hyperautomation tower — Agentic Process Automation, Digital Workforce & Multi-Agent Orchestration, Decision Intelligence Systems, Intelligent Document Processing as the usual core — sequenced through the Dataq Method with sector controls: PSD2 / PSD3 and instant payments obligations shape the design from the first sprint.

blocks.x: Two regimes anchor the control design here: PSD2 / PSD3 and instant payments and MiCA. Digital-asset exposure and service obligations where crypto-adjacent. Evidence for both is generated by the delivery itself — control tests, replay trails and documentation are artifacts of the program, not a reconstruction project.

Programs run on a fixed rhythm so progress is visible from week one. Weeks 1–2 lock the baseline: the current metric is measured with your team and signed before build starts. Weeks 3–8 deliver the pilot on bounded scope — one decision path, one workflow, one plant or one portfolio — with a control owner named on your side. Weeks 9–12 industrialize what worked: runbooks, monitoring, enablement and a measured delta against the signed baseline. Anything that misses its gate is stopped or redirected with a documented decision, not quietly extended.
